messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: net-high-latency us-east-6 (AZ6) — potential IPv6 connectivity failures, paging sam

sam: I got the page. seeing spikes and 502s for a handful of hosted API customers in us-east-6. IPv4 requests ok, IPv6 requests either hang or return early 504/502. looks like PMTUD or fragmentation issue. digging in.

maya: checking infra side — ML-serving nodes in AZ6 report lots of TCP retransmits on IPv6. BGP looks stable, routes unchanged. suspecting PMTUD blackhole when packets exceed ~1400 bytes.

sam: can you run a traceroute6 from edge into a failing host?

maya: attaching quick traceroute6 and tcpdump snippet: 

```
traceroute6 -n -f 1 -m 20 2600:1f18:abcd::12
1  fe80::1  0.23 ms
2  2001:db8:aaaa::1  1.12 ms
3  2001:db8:core::5  2.57 ms  (fragmentation-needed)
4  2600:1f18:abcd::12  10.5 ms

# tcpdump shows: ICMPv6 Packet too big (type2) not reaching source
14:22:10.123456 IP6 2600:... > 2600:...: IP6 (hlim 64,DF) 
14:22:10.123457 IP6 2600:... > 2600:...: ICMP6, destination unreachable, Packet too big, mtu=1280
```

maya: but the source host never receives the ICMP6 back. looks like something upstream or the cloud fabric dropping ICMPv6 PTB.

sam: that matches PMTUD blackhole. For IPv4, intermediate devices respond and MSS clamp works. For IPv6 nothing returns so hosts keep sending large segments.

jules: support reports ~3 paying customers affected (some SDK users) showing ~7-12% request failures in last 20m. customers using long prompts / streaming API most affected.

katie: quick mitigation idea: 1) apply MSS clamp on egress border for IPv6 2) enable IPv4-preferred on LB for fallback for flagged customers 3) reroute traffic from AZ6 -> AZ4 for heavy customers while we investigate.

maya: agree. I've prepared the config for MSS clamp (1420) on the AZ6 edge routers. Will push if we get ack. It should force endpoints to drop packet size and avoid PMTUD reliance.

sam: do it. Also reach out to cloud provider support - need to confirm if ICMPv6 PTB is being rate-limited or filtered inside AZ6 fabric.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued by maya: mss-clamp-az6/1 -> PROD (requires approval).

lee: +1 from net-eng. I'll open a cloud ticket with the provider and mention potential ICMPv6 filtering and recent jumbo-frame toggle in AZ6.

maya: applying MSS clamp now. command: 
```
# on edge router (example)
set firewall mss-clamp ipv6 1420
commit
```

maya: applied, monitoring throughput.

sam: initial numbers: error rate for affected customers dropped from ~10% to ~1.2% after clamp. Streaming still flaky for some sessions, but majority improved.

jules: informing customers: sent provisional note to the 3 affected accounts, offered reroute to us-east-4 for critical workloads. some asked for ETA.

raj: tracking customer impact: affected volume ~0.6% of overall requests in that region, but hits some low-latency SLAs. need incident severity update.

sam: SRE severity -> P2 (partial outage for specific customers) for now. continuing mitigation and provider engagement.

maya: cloud provider replied to initial ticket: they confirm a recent change in AZ6 load balancer that silently drops ICMPv6 PTB for certain ECMP paths when jumbo frames enabled on hosts. they asked for packet captures and impacted CIDRs.

lee: sent captures + sample failing connections, asked for configuration rollback. provider says they'll escalate to network infra team.

katie: in parallel I've flipped load-balancer preference for the flagged API routes to prefer IPv4 (config change) for customer keys we flagged. This should keep new sessions on IPv4.

sam: logging the temporary routing change: 
```
# LB rule snippet
- match: route_key in [list_of_keys] 
  action: prefer_ipv4
  ttl: 30m
```

sam: handoff — I'm on call for another page in 25m. Katie taking lead on mitigation and provider comms. Maya on network config/monitoring. Lee owns cloud ticket and escalation. Jules is customer comms. Raj looped for severity decisions.

katie: ack. I'll keep updating here and drop a short handoff summary at 1767206900 when sam hands off.

sam: thanks team, symptoms reduced but still watching. leaving notes for postmortem: root cause likely combination of provider change + jumbo-frame host setting + ICMPv6 PTB suppression causing PMTUD blackhole. temporary fixes: MSS clamp, lb IPv4-preference, reroute heavy customers.

katie: update at 1767205600: provider confirms they rolled back the change in AZ6 for the affected LB cluster. They report ICMPv6 PTB should now be forwarded. We're seeing additional reduction in failures.

maya: verified restored ICMP6 PTB flow — traceroute6 now shows proper ICMP reply and MTU negotiation. rolling back MSS clamp in 10m after monitoring.

sam: final numbers pre- and post-mitigation: 
- failures for affected keys: peak 12% -> after MSS clamp 1.2% -> after provider rollback 0.3%
- affected customers: 3 (notably one high-traffic SDK user)

jules: customers updated: two accepted reroute, one stayed on MSS-clamped path until rollback. all requested post-incident notes.

katie: rolling back IPv4-prefer LB rule for customers now that provider fixed fabric. will keep a short duration flag in case it reappears.

lee: cloud ticket escalated to Level 2 and is now resolved by provider for this incident. asked for RCA from provider.

maya: removing MSS clamp now. monitor window 20m.

deploy-bot: rollback executed: mss-clamp-az6/1 -> rollback -> SUCCESS.

sam: leaving oncall. handoff note at 1767206900: we mitigated via MSS clamp + LB IPv4 fallback + provider rollback. provider change caused ICMPv6 PTB suppression for some ECMP paths when jumbo frames enabled on hosts. severity P2. follow-ups: confirm provider RCA, consider infra guardrail to disable jumbo frames by default in AZ6, add PMTUD-blackhole detection alert.

katie: taking over oncall duties. I'll coordinate postmortem writeup with maya and lee.

jules: will draft customer-facing postmortem note and share.

raj: will add incident to weekly ops review and track any billing/credit requests.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status changed -> monitoring. assigned: katie.

sam: thanks all, nice run.

katie: will follow up with timeline and tentative RCA link here once provider sends full details.
